comments.value: @{60e65f577ae9d0492b0f2a75|full_name} I'm having some trouble reproducing this issue on a fresh avatar project. Any chance you could share an affected avatar ID?

@{654a7d1f1870ff9faf0911e8|full_name} I'm sorry. I missed a majar detail. It's not avatar based. Every avatar of mine with "-" in parameters had this issue. even new and fresh uploaded avatars (test avatar i initially made for it too: https://vrchat.com/home/avatar/avtr_3ba27dc4-4469-4580-951a-dde2bc9db2aa). I tested this for 4h before i was like "na something is off. this is not me. i make a report". A bit later i restarted VRChat and it was gone.

@{60e65f577ae9d0492b0f2a75|full_name} Thanks for the update. I noticed that in the avatar you linked, the parameters you noted in the log are used by parameter drivers, but not specifically included in the avatar descriptor. That should be fine, but it could be a clue. Do any of the parameters in the descriptor that have dashes also show up in the log? (i.e "ObjectTracking/LHR-32E2511E/RRY-Bit6")

It occurs to me that since this avatar relies on parameters that are defined in the animations themselves, they wouldn't get defined if the animations we unable to load. (For example, if custom animations were blocked by shield settings.) Any chance that could be the culprit here?

@{654a7d1f1870ff9faf0911e8|full_name} 

I might have copying the wrong expression parameter list into the new project for the test avatar. I hope it's okay to add another (more complex) avatar to explain the situation.

The Avatar i use for *my* testing is https://vrchat.com/home/avatar/avtr_7745c998-f68f-4e69-87df-956ea2ed4b5f

Expression Parameters and Animator Parameters are matching (verified, see screenshot). I initially used this variables only with parameter drivers. after a while i added a toggle to the menue called "LHB-486E0CD4" (toggling ObjectTracking/config/LHB-486E0CD4) to verify it's not an parameter driver issue. I could have only created this toggle if the parameter also is in the parameter list (verfied, i added 2 screenshots to verify that my project is not broke and an unknown parameter would block me from uploading). The Last Update on that Avatar is 08/07/2024, 22:10:05 (15 minutes before, the log posted above from 2024.07.08 22:23:29) (I verified that times are in my timezone and are not a mix)

"LHB-074BE18A" must be from a before uploaded avatar with same ID. (Could try to verfiy if needed)

I couldn't find "LHR-32E2511E" in the same log.

@{654a7d1f1870ff9faf0911e8|full_name}

> It occurs to me that since this avatar relies on parameters that are defined in the animations themselves, they wouldn't get defined if the animations we unable to load. (For example, if custom animations were blocked by shield settings.) Any chance that could be the culprit here?

I think no. I'm not aware that i'm able to shild block myself

And even if you would be right, why were parameters like "ObjectTracking/Playspace/LPX" working? (same behaviour in my animator/avatar, just without "-")

@{60e65f577ae9d0492b0f2a75|full_name}: "ObjectTracking/Playspace/LPX-Bit0" doesn't appear in the log either, so I'm still not sure the "-" is the key.

Since all the parameters in the log contain "LHB-074BE18A", I suspect you're right that some data from an older version of the avatar is getting cached and reapplied. (Especially considering that a restart fixed the issue.) 

Are those parameter names being generated somehow? Could they all be replaced between avatar revisions?

@{654a7d1f1870ff9faf0911e8|full_name}

> "ObjectTracking/Playspace/LPX-Bit0" doesn't appear in the log either, so I'm still not sure the "-" is the key.

"ObjectTracking/Playspace/LPX-Bit0" will never exist (logic wise).

You are still right. "ObjectTracking/Playspace/RPX-Bit0" does exist on that avatar and is not listed in any error message.

> Are those parameter names being generated somehow?

Yes, ex LHB-074BE18A is a serial number. Limited to a-zA-Z-

> Could they all be replaced between avatar revisions?

Yes, they could but not automatic and not that day. I would have to enter a different serial number and to press a button to update the avatar with the new serial number. It's very likely that i used a different tracker with serial number "LHB-074BE18A" before. but i haven't changed the serial number between uploads on the day i had this issue.

> I suspect you're right that some data from an older version of the avatar is getting cached and reapplied.

I guess then it was the config which was in cache on disk when the avatar got loaded the first time and than never got updated with any new downloaded avatar version. I think i uploaded 3-5 versions that day.

@{60e65f577ae9d0492b0f2a75|full_name}: I asked around and got a little more context on the OSC config json. As a compromise to allow the config json to be manually added, the endpoints will not automatically update when parameters are added to/removed from a given avatar. I suspect that we've been chasing a red herring, and that the endpoints you had cached for this avatar were just out of date.

I'll pass this along to the other devs. Maybe that workflow can be improved a bit. Thanks for helping me get to the bottom of this!

details:
1. use an avatar with "-" in variable name

2. change the value (Avatar Parameter driver or via expression menu)

Expected behaviour:

While listening on port 9001 or on our OSCQuery Port we should recieve a message with the update. 

Current behaviour:

No message for parameter containing "-" (ex: "AA-BB"), others are working.
